sentences.text: My name is Emma, and I want to help you with your writing.
Today, we are going to learn a way to organize your writing to help you with your essays, with things like TOEFL, IELTS, or even university and high school essays.
So what we're talking about is something called the PEEL framework.
So, the first thing I want you to do is forget using AI to write your essays.
You can do this. You can write.
So, let me teach you about PEEL and how it can help you with your writing.
PEEL stands for point, example, explain, and link.
We're going to look at each of these parts of PEEL in more detail, and then we're going to look at some example paragraphs.
I can't wait. I love using PEEL, and I think you will, too.
So, the P in PEEL stands for point.
So, what is the point of what you're writing?
So, we often use PEEL when we're writing paragraphs, especially paragraphs where we're trying to make an argument or to give our opinion on something.
So, when I'm talking about point, what I'm really saying is the first sentence you state the main idea.
So, here's an example of how you might start off an essay.
So, imagine somebody asks you to write about exercise and students.
Your point might be, "Exercise is important for students because it improves both their physical and mental health."
Okay, so that's an example of a topic sentence, and these are just some words that can be helpful when you write, when you're giving the point.
"I think that." "I think that exercise is very important for students."
"One important idea is exercise can help students' mental or physical health."
"In my opinion, exercise is critical for student well-being."
Exercise for students is important because it helps them physically and mentally.
So, there's some different examples of how to use these types of words.
They're great words at the start of a paragraph, especially for IELTS, TOEFL, and high school paragraphs.
So, now let's look at the "E" in PEEL.
The first "E" in PEEL stands for "example".
So, you've already given your point, now you need to back it up with an example.
So, give evidence or an example to prove your point.
So, here are some great words that you can use to help you do this.
You can say "for example", "for instance".
"One example is..."
"This can be seen when..."
So, going back to our exercise point, my point was that exercise is important for students' physical and mental well-being, so that's my point.
"For example, regular exercise can reduce stress and increase energy levels."
So, I'm giving a real example to support my point.
So, you give the point, then you follow it up with an example.
All right, let's see what the next "E" in the PEEL method means.
The next "E" in PEEL, so the second "E", stands for "explain".
So, the next thing you do when you're writing a paragraph is you explain your example more deeply, so you go into more detail.
Here are some words that can be helpful for that.
"This means that..."
"As a result..." "Because of this..."
"This helps because..."

So, going back to our example from the beginning where I mentioned exercise is important for students' physical and mental well-being, and then I gave an example about how exercise can help with energy, now I'm going to talk about that a little bit more.
So, as a result, students often feel more focused and perform better in class, so I'm giving more detail from the previous example.
And that's what you want to do.
So, you give an example, for instance, and then you give more detail or more of an explanation.
All right, and we will look at more examples in a moment, but let's now get to the final letter in PEEL, which is the "L".
What does "L" stand for?
So, the "L" in PEEL stands for "link".
You need to link back to the main point, so you've done your point, you've given an example, you've explained your example, and now it's time to go back and link it back to the initial point.
So, these are some great words to do that.
"Therefore", "for this reason", "overall", "this shows that".
So let's look at an example of this.
Going back to our original point about exercise, the very last thing I can write is "Therefore, exercise can help students succeed both academically and personally."
So now let's look at the whole paragraph together so you can see how well it flows when you use the PEEL method.
All right. So now let's look at the whole paragraph.
Exercise is important for students because it improves both physical and mental health.
For example, regular exercise can reduce stress and increase energy level.
As a result, students often feel more focused and perform better in class.
Therefore, exercise can help students succeed both academically and personally.
Boom. Great paragraph. All right, so now let's look at another example paragraph we can write together.
All right, so let's practice another paragraph together.

All right. So let's look at what the paragraph says, and then you can organize it in the correct way.

One major benefit of public transportation is reduced traffic congestion.
For example, cities such as Tokyo have efficient subway systems used by millions daily.

What's the example given?
Where is the explanation for the example?

What's the link?
